aiOverview.content: In November 2017, U.S. Senator Rand Paul was attacked by his neighbor, Rene Boucher, while doing yard work at his Kentucky home, resulting in six broken ribs and lung injuries. The 2017 assault, driven by a property line dispute, led to Boucher pleading guilty to assaulting a member of Congress, serving 30 days in prison, and paying over $580,000 in damages. Key Details of the 2017 Attack The Assailant: Rene Boucher, a retired physician and next-door neighbor, tackled Paul from behind. Injuries: Paul suffered six broken ribs and, subsequently, pneumonia. Legal Outcome: Boucher was sentenced to 30 days in prison, fined $10,000, and later ordered to pay over $580,000 in damages, including punitive damages and compensation for pain and suffering. Motive: The attack was reportedly sparked by a long-running dispute over property maintenance and yard waste. Recent Developments (March 2026) During a March 18, 2026, Senate committee hearing, Senator Paul confronted Markwayne Mullin, a nominee for Secretary of Homeland Security, for past comments where Mullin stated he "understood" why the 2017 attack occurred, according to BBC. Paul criticized Mullin for justifying the violence against him, arguing it raised questions about Mullin's fitness to lead the Department of Homeland Security. Mullin did not apologize, claiming he was being direct, per The New York Times. Other IncidentsIn 2023, a staffer for Senator Paul was also violently attacked in Washington, D.C., as reported by NPR.
